lesson:
Review round 1 (quality lens) accepted two findings; fix exactly these. (1) P1 CLAIM RACE — pending-interaction-prompt-binding.ts:99: the prompt is bound (made visible and claimable) FIRST and only afterwards are batch members updated one by one to eligible=false, so a callback can claim a rendered remember code before the first update lands and settlement reads a still-eligible context; a failed update also leaves a bound prompt partially finalized. Fix: finalize every batch member's context (eligible=false) BEFORE the prompt row is persisted/bound — run the member updates first, and if any update returns false, return false without binding (nothing partially finalized is ever claimable); if the durability port offers a way to do the member updates and the binding in one transaction, prefer that; individual prompts stay untouched. Add a test in pending-interaction-durability.test.ts proving the members are ineligible before the prompt becomes claimable and that a failed member update leaves the prompt unbound. (2) P2 — runtime/permission-remember-settlement.ts:43: the boolean from persistPermissionRememberPromptContext is ignored and the requester delegates to the approval flow even when the durable member was not updated, so a remember option could settle as its scalar decision while silently failing to learn. Fix: treat a false result as a persistence failure BEFORE exposing the prompt — do not delegate; surface it the same way the durable flow already surfaces a failed pending-interaction persistence (the existing DurableInteractionPersistenceError path), so the prompt is never shown without its context. Add the case to the IPC suite. Then re-run the twelve leaves, tsc, check:architecture, prettier; do not run npm test in the sandbox (EMFILE) — the host does.
(3) P2 from the performance lens — the batch path awaits updatePendingInteractionPayload once per member (N serialized round trips after the binding query). Finalize all affected member payloads in ONE bulk repository operation — extend the durability port with a single batch update (the Postgres implementation issues one statement; the in-memory fakes implement the same method) — ideally inside the same transaction that binds the prompt, so (1) and (3) are solved together: one atomic step makes every batch member ineligible and binds the prompt, or does neither. Per-member loops are not acceptable on this path.
(4) P2 from the security lens — worker-coordination-permission-prompt.postgres.ts:47: the mapper skips parsePermissionDecisionCode when claim_mode is an empty string (a truthiness check), so a claimed row with '' passes the null-only completeness check and returns intent.mode as a runtime null through a non-null assertion. Fix: test explicitly for null before parsing and route every non-null string, including '', through the codec so an empty or unknown claim_mode is REFUSED (fail closed); add the empty-string case to the Postgres suite's malformed-claim leaf.
